doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: The Adderley brothers meet Erskine Hawkins' band
summary: Two young players, Cannonball and Nat Adderley, sat in with the Hawkins band in Orlando and were soon discovered.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Please do, believe me. The Adderley brothers are my heroes. I love them.

Yeah. Well Nat and I, we did Orlando, Florida last year at Disneyland. He and I. Two cornet players, trumpet players. But during one night in Orlando, Florida, these two little kids came up to Erskine, and the place was packed. And these two little kids had their horns. So one of them said, “Could we play some?” Now this is during the bebop days. This is 1950, 1952. And we had Sonny Payne in the band. As a matter of fact, in the fifties the Erskine Hawkins band went out of business. And that was the best that we’ve ever played together. But things had gotten worse economically and everything. So we said okay, we’ll let them play some. Man, these two kids, Cannon and the little cornet player, oh they played, this was something to hear. And the next thing you know, they were on big time. And there’s a story out that they never had to audition, they never had to do anything. The story is that one night, on Boston Road in the Bronx, Nancy Wilson was singing and these two guys had a little gig for about twenty dollars, and someone from Capitol Records came in and heard them. They never looked back. You know what I mean? They both was very well educated. Florida A & M has a great reputation scholastically.
